children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares fell on Monday as concerns over the AI trade intensified ahead of earnings from megacap tech companies this week. The won strengthened, while the benchmark bond yield fell.
** The benchmark KOSPI
was down 83.14 points, or 1.50%, at 5,467.16 as of 03:30 GMT. The index has risen about 30% so far this year.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
fell 1.39%, while peer SK Hynix
lost 0.47%.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 1.70%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were down 2.71% and down 1.78%, respectively.
** This week, about one-third of S&P 500 companies report quarterly results, including Alphabet
, Microsoft
and Amazon
, three AI hyperscalers whose capital spending forecasts will be closely watched on Wall Street.

** SK Hynix said it will announce shareholder return measures on Wednesday when the South Korean chipmaker releases quarterly results, responding to a report that it is considering a special dividend of about 16 trillion won ($12 billion).
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 0.91%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
fell 0.34%.
** Of the total 914 traded issues, 98 shares advanced, while 792 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 517.9 billion won.
** The won was quoted at 1,322.0 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.32% higher than its previous close at 1,326.2.
** The currency has strengthened about 9% against the dollar so far this year.
** In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.09 point to 103.24.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 2.4 basis points to 3.792%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 1.9 bps to 4.080%.
